subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Irish Coffee: A Foggy Night in Foynes
description: A quick win: understand Irish Coffee: A Foggy Night in Foynes.

hook.text: Irish coffee was invented in 1943 at a windswept airport in Foynes, Ireland—to warm shivering transatlantic passengers.

buildup.text: Chef Joe Sheridan added whiskey to hot coffee, topped with cream, for passengers whose flight turned back in bad weather.

discovery.text: When a passenger asked 'Is this Brazilian coffee?' Sheridan replied: 'No, it's Irish coffee.' The name stuck forever.

twist.text: Journalist Stanton Delaplane brought the recipe to San Francisco's Buena Vista Café in 1952. It became iconic.

climax.text: The Buena Vista still serves 2,000 Irish coffees daily—the most of any single bar in the world. Sheridan's creation endures.

punchline.text: Bad weather, warm whiskey, floating cream. One stormy night created a global classic.

quiz.question: Where was Irish coffee invented?
options: Foynes airport, Ireland — to warm shivering transatlantic passengers in 1943

details.summary: Irish coffee was created in 1943 by chef Joe Sheridan at Foynes airport in Ireland to warm cold, weary transatlantic passengers. He combined hot coffee, Irish whiskey, brown sugar, and cream into a layered drink. Travel writer Stanton Delaplane later introduced it to San Francisco.
details.whyItMatters: Irish coffee shows how a simple improvisation at a remote airport became one of the world's most recognized cocktail-style coffee drinks.
takeaways: Joe Sheridan created Irish coffee at Foynes airport in 1943
It was made to warm cold transatlantic flight passengers
San Francisco's Buena Vista Cafe popularized it in America

faq.question: What is the proper way to make a traditional Irish coffee?
faq.answer: Pre-warm a glass, add hot black coffee and a spoonful of brown sugar, stir to dissolve, add a shot of Irish whiskey, and float lightly whipped cream on top by pouring over the back of a spoon. Do not stir after adding cream.

faq.question: How did Irish coffee travel from a small Irish airport to global fame?
faq.answer: Travel writer Stanton Delaplane tasted it at Foynes and brought the recipe to the Buena Vista Cafe in San Francisco in 1952. The cafe perfected the technique and has since served over 40 million Irish coffees.
